findings.evidence: Proof body: first `rintro ⟨hl, hr⟩` block never mentions `hc`; second uses `hc.left.mul_left_eq_zero_iff` twice. The sibling lemma in this same file, `eq_zero_of_isSymm_of_isAlt` (line 41), deliberately carries `IsLeftRegular (2 : R)`, and the module doc (lines 17-19) states that carrying exactly the needed regularity is the point.
findings.fix: Weaken the binder to `(hc : IsLeftRegular c)` and replace `hc.left` by `hc` — `IsLeftRegular.mul_left_eq_zero_iff` (Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Regular.lean:88) needs only `MulZeroClass`. Optionally split off the hypothesis-free forward implication as `Nondegenerate.of_smul`.
findings.issue: `nondegenerate_smul_iff` assumes `IsRegular c`, but the proof only ever uses `hc.left` (lines 65, 68); the `IsRightRegular` conjunct is visibly unused. The `←` direction needs left-regularity; the `→` direction (lines 56-61) uses no hypothesis at all.

findings.evidence: Mathlib defines `Nondegenerate B := SeparatingLeft B ∧ SeparatingRight B` (SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean:594) and consistently states the one-sided lemmas first, deriving the two-sided one — e.g. `Nondegenerate.congr := ⟨h.1.congr .., h.2.congr ..⟩` and `SeparatingRight.congr := SeparatingLeft.congr (B := B.flip)` (ibid. 618-625). This repo's `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Isometry.lean:296,350,393,402` takes `hB : B.SeparatingLeft`, not `Nondegenerate`, as its working hypothesis.
findings.fix: State `separatingLeft_smul_iff` (and get the right-hand version via `B.flip`), then define `nondegenerate_smul_iff := ⟨...⟩` as their conjunction, following Mathlib's own pattern.
findings.issue: The result is stated only for the two-sided `Nondegenerate`, so the same two-line argument is written out four times and a caller holding only `B.SeparatingLeft` cannot get `(c • B).SeparatingLeft`. No symmetry is assumed here, so left- and right-separation are genuinely independent.

summary: The lattice-level API sits at the natural level and negation is properly derived from scaling. The new general lemma `TauCeti.BilinForm.nondegenerate_smul_iff` carries a stronger regularity hypothesis than its proof uses and is stated only in the two-sided form, blocking the one-sided `SeparatingLeft` users this repo already has.
